title: Loss of Datalink Log-On in Oceanic Airspace — Crew Procedure

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Crew procedure for a lost datalink log-on in oceanic airspace, covering the waiting period before a manual log-on, the reversion to voice and the position reporting that must continue meanwhile.

sections.purpose: Gives the flight crew the actions to take when the datalink log-on is lost in oceanic airspace, and the reporting obligations that continue while it is unavailable.
sections.description: A lost log-on in oceanic airspace removes the primary means of communication with the service unit and, on most oceanic tracks, the means by which position reports are made. The crew see the communication page change to not connected and, on most occasions, no other indication. The aircraft will attempt to re-establish the log-on on its own, and in most cases succeeds within a few minutes. Until it does, the aircraft is not in datalink contact and the service unit is not receiving position reports. That is the operationally significant part: the airspace requires a report at each waypoint and the absence of one will be treated as a communication failure by the service unit before the crew are aware of any problem. The crew must therefore start voice reporting rather than wait indefinitely for the automatic recovery, and must tell the service unit what has happened so that the missed report is not escalated.
sections.crew_procedure: Note the time at which the page showed not connected. Continue to fly the cleared track and maintain the cleared level; a communication loss is not a clearance loss. Wait the period given in the operations manual for the automatic recovery. If the page has not returned to connected, log on again manually. If the manual log-on fails, select the long range voice frequency for the sector and make a voice position report, stating that datalink is unavailable and giving the time of the last successful exchange. Continue voice reporting at each waypoint until the log-on is re-established. Record the occurrence in the technical log with the time and the position.

type_data.crew_action: Wait for automatic recovery, then log on manually; if unsuccessful, revert to long range voice and report by voice at each waypoint.
